channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Hello Houston (February 3, 2026)
item.description: Today: We learn about Broadway at the Hobby Center’s upcoming 2026-27 Season, talk with Ebony Williams about running for judge of Harris County Civil Court at Law No. 2, and media executive Amy DuBois Barnett discusses her debut novel.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 3, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters – we have “The Commuter Cut” – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Artemis II’s lunar mission is delayed to March after problems in NASA’s dress rehearsal
item.description: During the two-day dress rehearsal, running through launch-day procedures, crews found a liquid hydrogen leak in part of the rocket.

item.title: Maine plane crash victims worked for luxury travel startup led by Houston lawyer
item.description: The six people killed in the Jan. 25 plane crash included an acclaimed chef, a sommelier and an event planner working for Tara Arnold, a Houston lawyer-turned-entrepreneur and philanthropist. Local police confirmed the death of Arnold and three of the others on Tuesday.

item.title: Houston-area winter temperatures are trending warmer, despite recent cold snaps
item.description: The five warmest Februarys on record for Houston have all occurred since 2012, according to National Weather Service data.

item.title: Amid financial crunch, Houston police and fire projected to overshoot OT budgets by more than $50 million
item.description: Police and fire department officials attributed the excess overtime spending to an inadequate number of personnel and unexpected weather events.

item.title: NTSB report cites low visibility, miscommunication before fatal Galveston plane crash
item.description: The small Mexican Navy plane crashed into the Galveston Bay in late December 2025, killing six people and injuring two others.

item.title: Siemens Energy to expand Houston facilities
item.description: The company is investing $1 billion in its U.S. facilities, including $23 million in Texas.

item.title: Blue Origin’s lunar lander is at Houston’s Johnson Space Center for testing
item.description: The private space exploration company announced the lunar lander’s arrival in Houston. Now, it will undergo testing in space-like conditions.

item.title: Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo says she always planned to endorse Al Green in TX-18 election
item.description: In an interview with Houston Public Media on Tuesday, she said she's worked with Green since she was first elected to office.
